A typical case

Illustrative example

The context
A video game publisher reads reactions to its beta.
What the conversation showed
The story and graphics are praised; microtransactions and lag concentrate the criticism.

Our recommendation

Fix the lag before release and rethink the pricing model.

04

Our approach to this case

We read the unfiltered verdict on your products and your competitors': reviews, test videos, forums, workarounds. An analyst ranks strengths and irritants by frequency, product by product, and turns them into priorities for the next version.

  1. 1Framing

    We choose the products to evaluate, yours and competitors'.

  2. 2Collection

    We collect everything said about each one.

  3. 3Analysis

    An analyst ranks strengths and irritants, product by product.

  4. 4Decision

    We hand you a verdict and improvement priorities.

What we read

  • Product reviewsRetail sites, comparison sites, specialist forums.
  • Review videosTests and unboxings on YouTube and TikTok.
  • Social networksReal uses and users' workarounds.
  • CompetitorsThe same sources, for their products.
05

Frequently asked questions

Can you evaluate a product not yet released?

Yes, from reactions to a beta, a teaser or competing products already on the market.

How many reviews does it take?

A few hundred are often enough to see patterns; we tell you if the volume is too low.

Do you cover reviews abroad?

Yes, in more than twenty languages.
